newsitem.title: KENYA: Burundi to stage "national debate" next month.
newsitem.headline: Burundi to stage "national debate" next month.

text.p: Burundi's military government said on Thursday it would stage the first round of a national debate on the country's future next month but it said Hutu rebels would be excluded.
The debate would be key to a three-year transitional process aimed at reviving democracy in the war-torn country, said Jean-Luc Ndizeye, spokesman for military leader Pierre Buyoya.
The first round of the debate would be limited to legalised political parties and civil societies and no agenda has been set.

"Next month we are going to start a national debate. All the political leaders will be invited but if one wants to talk in the debate one has to stop killing civilians," Ndizeye said by telephone from the Burundian capital Bujumbura.
"We don't want them (Hutu rebels) at this stage," Ndizeye said, adding that holding talks with rebels remained integral to the government's programme.
A national debate was integral to U.N. plans for Burundi prior to a coup last July, but analysts said it could prove little more than a talking shop without rebel participation.
Buyoya came to power in a coup by the Tutsi-led army outlining an ambitious transitional process and claiming only he could stop Burundi from sliding into genocide.
Ndizeye blamed sanctions imposed by regional states after the coup for delaying implementation of the debate originally scheduled for last November.
The states led by Tanzania and Kenya set unconditional talks with Hutu rebels as a condition for ending the blockade.
Around 150,000 people have died in Burundi's ethnic conflict since 1993 and human rights groups say abuses have worsened since the coup.
